required_outcomes: Does not leave the report unanswered behind the closure: reopens this request or records the tenant's report against it.

Asks the tenant what the machine is doing now, in particular whether it is the same problem of the water not heating on the 60°C cycle or something different (with any error code or other symptom), because that decides whether Lantern Services return under their guarantee or a new call-out needs the landlord's approval.
Acknowledges the report to the tenant and says what happens once he replies, without inventing a visit date.
acceptable_alternatives: Alerting Lantern Services that a return visit under their guarantee may be needed and asking for their availability, alongside the question to the tenant, provided nothing chargeable is instructed.
Informing the landlord (Mercer) that the tenant has reported a further problem and that details are being confirmed, provided the earlier repair is not described as failed before the tenant confirms.
positive_behaviours: Keeps the question short and specific, suited to a reply from a phone.
Schedules a follow-up in case the tenant does not reply.
Notes that the £75.11 invoice should not be treated as settled until the nature of the problem is known.
red_flags: Escalating to a human because the report is vague.
Asking the landlord to approve a new chargeable call-out as if no repair had just been done.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant the job is complete or closed and that he must raise a new request.
Approving a chargeable visit or quote without the landlord's agreement.
critical_failures: Leaving the tenant's report unactioned with the case closed.
